subject: Applied Calculus
unit: Unit II — Functions of Several Variables
sourceBasis: ACADRIX MA25C01 Unit II notes: partial derivatives, chain rule, total derivative/differential, maxima and minima of two variables, Lagrange multipliers and engineering applications.
note: Original ACADRIX exam-practice problems; not claimed official university questions or verified PYQs.

questions.question: For a given function of two or three variables, determine the required first- and higher-order partial derivatives and verify equality of mixed partial derivatives where applicable.
solutionPlan: Differentiate with respect to one variable while holding the others constant.
Compute the mixed derivatives in both orders.
Compare the results and state the conclusion.

questions.question: Use the multivariable chain rule to find the derivative of a composite function when its variables depend on a common parameter.
Given z=f(x,y), with x and y defined in terms of one or more independent variables, obtain the required first derivative using the multivariable chain rule.
solutionPlan: Draw or identify the variable dependency.
Apply dz/dt=f_x dx/dt+f_y dy/dt or the corresponding multivariable form.

questions.question: Find the total derivative of a multivariable function and explain the contribution of each independent variable to the total change.
solutionPlan: Identify the independent and dependent variables.
Substitute given rates or increments when supplied.

questions.question: Use the total differential to approximate the change in the value of a function of two variables for small changes in its independent variables.
solutionPlan: Evaluate derivatives at the specified point.
Interpret df as the first-order approximation.

questions.question: Determine the local maxima, local minima and saddle points of a function of two variables using first- and second-derivative tests.
solutionPlan: Solve f_x=0 and f_y=0 for stationary points.
Classify each stationary point using D and f_xx.

questions.question: Apply the second-derivative test to classify the stationary points of a specified two-variable function.
solutionPlan: Evaluate the second partial derivatives at each point.
Use the sign conditions to classify maximum, minimum or saddle point.

questions.question: Find the constrained maximum and minimum values of a function of two variables subject to a specified equality constraint using Lagrange multipliers.
solutionPlan: Solve the resulting equations together with the constraint.
Evaluate f at all feasible candidates.

questions.question: Use Lagrange multipliers to optimize a function of three variables subject to a constraint.
solutionPlan: Compare objective values and state the optimum.

questions.question: Formulate and solve a two-variable engineering optimization problem involving a physical quantity subject to a design constraint.
solutionPlan: Translate the physical constraint into an equation.
Apply ordinary stationary-point analysis or Lagrange multipliers as appropriate.
Interpret the optimum in engineering terms.

questions.question: Use first-order multivariable approximation through the total differential to estimate the value of a function near a known operating point.
solutionPlan: Evaluate the function and first partial derivatives there.
State the estimated value and approximation assumption.

questions.question: A physical quantity is expressed as a function of several intermediate variables. Differentiate it with respect to time using the complete chain rule.
Find all stationary points of a two-variable function and determine whether each point corresponds to a maximum, minimum or saddle point.
solutionPlan: Set both first partial derivatives equal to zero.
Evaluate the second-derivative criterion at every point.
Classify and present the results systematically.

questions.question: Explain and demonstrate how a constraint changes an unconstrained optimization problem into a constrained optimization problem, then solve a representative case using Lagrange multipliers.
solutionPlan: Interpret the role of the constraint.

questions.question: Solve a complete multivariable-calculus problem requiring partial derivatives, chain rule or total differential, followed by a stationary-point or constrained-optimization decision.
solutionPlan: Solve the optimization portion and check candidates.
Present the final mathematical and engineering interpretation.

examChecklist: Hold other variables constant when taking a partial derivative.
Track every dependency in a multivariable chain rule.
Use df=f_x dx+f_y dy for first-order change estimates.
For two-variable stationary points, compute D=f_xx f_yy-(f_xy)^2.
For Lagrange multipliers, solve the gradient equations together with the constraint.
Compare all feasible candidates before declaring a constrained maximum or minimum.
For engineering problems, state the meaning and units of the optimum.
